headline: You can visit Bhutan without any sponsor. Book a 2-3 week guided trip for late March to April 2027, while the US$100-per-person-per-night fee is still guaranteed (it runs to Aug 31, 2027). A longer stay needs one of three things: a Bhutanese friend who really knows you (about 30 days), a genuine volunteer or work role, or the still-unconfirmed Gelephu nomad residence.
key_points: You can visit without any sponsor. A tourist visa needs no host. Apply yourselves through bhutan.travel/visa, or let a licensed tour operator or hotel apply for you. The visa costs US$40 each, paid once and non-refundable, and is reviewed within 5 working days. You can stay up to 90 days from entry. Plan for each passport to have 6 months left after you leave (confirm with your tour operator).

The main cost is the Sustainable Development Fee (SDF), a daily tourism fee. It is US$100 per adult per night, so US$200 a night for the two of you, and you pay it in full with the visa. The US$100 rate is guaranteed only until Aug 31, 2027. After that Bhutan may go back to its US$200 base rate per person. Nothing has been announced.

The best fit is a 2-3 week guided trip in late March to April 2027, while your designer starts on the house. The best seasons are spring (March to mid-April) and autumn (late September to November). The monsoon runs late June to September. Autumn 2027 falls after the fee guarantee ends, so spring 2027 is your window at today's rate. Paro Tshechu, a major festival, is tentatively set for Mar 18-22, 2027. It fits only if the land closes by early March.

You can leave for the spring 2027 trip with no permit deadline running, because the plans are still being drawn. Keep your belongings in a storage unit in town for this trip, since the lot has no permits yet. A longer stay fits best from 2029, after the house's final inspection. A long trip in the middle of the build works only right after a passed inspection, for under about 5 months, with any permit extension approved in writing first.

You can set your own pace with a licensed guide and a hired car with a driver. The official FAQ says the guide must be with you at all times, and there are no self-drive rentals. A tour operator is optional. Tourists may sleep only in hotels, village homestays or campsites certified by the Department of Tourism. A notice dated Aug 26, 2026 repeats that overnight stays at private homes or uncertified places are prohibited. The provider faces a fine of Nu. 50,000 (Bhutanese ngultrum) per service.

In Bhutan, a 'sponsor' means the host behind a non-tourist visa. That can be a government agency, a registered company or nonprofit, a school, or a Bhutanese friend for a personal-guest visa. Nobody can legitimately sell sponsorship. Treat any offer to sponsor you, or to sell you a guest letter, for a fee as a scam.

Only Bhutanese citizens who live in Bhutan can host a personal guest, and only someone they genuinely know. Reported limits are 2 guests per host per year and 30 days per visit, with the SDF waived. That is shorter than a tourist stay, and the two of you would use up a host's whole yearly allowance. You need this visa to stay at a friend's home. These details are unconfirmed (ask your host to check the current Department of Immigration requirements).

For a stay of months, a 90-day tourist visa costs about US$18,000 in SDF alone for the two of you. The other route is a genuine volunteer, teaching or work role with a registered Bhutanese organization. Bhutan's Prime Minister said in April 2023 that the SDF does not apply to non-tourist travel. The current rules are unconfirmed (ask the host organization to confirm with the Department of Immigration). Expect months of lead time.

Gelephu Mindfulness City (GMC) offers a Digital Nomad Residence. It costs US$2,800 a year plus a US$10,000 refundable deposit, held as a gold-backed token at DK Bank. It lasts 12 months and can be renewed to 24. A private company, NomadClub, sells it, and the GMC Authority has not published the rules. The SDF waiver and whether it covers a spouse are unconfirmed (ask info@gmc.bt before paying).

Budget about US$300-450 per person per day all-in. That covers the SDF, guide, car, 3-star lodging and meals. For two people, 2 weeks costs about US$8,400-12,600 on the ground, or about US$11,000-18,000 with flights (estimates). Each extra week adds about US$4,200-6,300 for two (estimate).

Paro is Bhutan's only international airport. From California, connect through Bangkok, Delhi or Kathmandu, with a night's stop on the way. Allow a spare day each way for weather. Reconfirm Drukair flights 72 hours ahead. Drukair allows 32 kg per checked bag.

Travel insurance has not been required since Apr 23, 2024. Medical and evacuation cover is still wise, because advanced care is limited outside Thimphu. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) page, updated Aug 25, 2026, makes four health points. Get hepatitis A and typhoid vaccines. Get the Japanese encephalitis vaccine for stays of a month or more. Talk to your doctor about rabies. Malaria is a risk in some areas (ask a travel clinic which ones).

risks.risk: The US$100 rate ends Aug 31, 2027 and may go back to US$200 per person. A delay in closing or design that pushes the trip later could double the fee.
risks.mitigation: Aim for late March to April 2027, or budget US$400 a night for two after the cutoff. Ask hosts@tourism.gov.bt in writing how nights after the cutoff are charged. Check bhutan.travel/announcements on Mar 1, 2027.

risks.risk: Paid 'sponsor' offers, fake personal-guest letters and hijacked websites can all cost you money, expose a host to fines, and lead to visa refusals later. For example, bhutancanada.org now shows an online casino.
risks.mitigation: Use only real friendships, registered organizations and licensed operators found through services.bhutan.travel. Never pay anyone for a letter. Reach organizations through email addresses confirmed by phone or referral. Never enter personal details on a page you did not expect to see.

risks.risk: The Gelephu nomad residence is sold by a private company. Neither the government nor the GMC Authority has published its rules. The US$10,000 deposit is held as a gold-backed token, and the SDF waiver and spouse coverage are unconfirmed.
risks.mitigation: Move no money until info@gmc.bt confirms in writing. Ask how and when the deposit is refunded, and what token or currency risk you would carry.

risks.risk: No primary source confirms the personal-guest and non-tourist visa rules, and a May 2026 requirements document may have changed them. Staying with a friend on a tourist visa breaks the certified-lodging rule and exposes your friend to fines.
risks.mitigation: Ask your host, organization or operator to download the current Department of Immigration documents before you rely on any of these rules. As tourists, stay only in certified hotels or homestays.

risks.risk: Time away from Yucca Valley can stall the build. A missed inspection can let a permit lapse, and the trailer, pods and stored belongings sit unattended.
risks.mitigation: Take the spring 2027 trip before any permit is issued. Later, leave only right after a passed inspection, for under about 5 months, with any extension approved in writing. Line up a caretaker or neighbor check-ins before you book flights.

risks.risk: Health and weather: rabies from dogs, malaria in some areas, and altitude (Paro and Thimphu sit at about 2,200-2,600 m, or 7,200-8,500 ft). Care is limited outside Thimphu, and weather delays at Paro can cause missed connections.
risks.mitigation: See a travel clinic 6-8 weeks before you leave. Buy cover that includes medical evacuation, and carry your prescriptions. Add a spare day at each connecting city, and reconfirm Drukair flights 72 hours ahead.

questions_for_couple: What does each of us want from Bhutan: a 2-3 week trip, a retreat, a skills exchange, or a months-long trial of living there?
Do we go in late March to April 2027 at US$200 a night for both of us, right after closing on the land? Or do we wait until 2029 and risk paying double?
What is our ceiling for Bhutan spending, given that 2 weeks for two is about US$11,000-18,000 with flights?
How do we feel about having a guide with us every day and sleeping only in certified hotels or homestays?
Do we genuinely know a Bhutanese citizen who lives in Bhutan? Would it feel right to ask them to use their whole yearly guest allowance on us?
Would we take on a real volunteer or work role, with its schedule and duties, so we can stay longer without the daily fee?
Who checks on the land and our stored belongings while we are away, and what is our rule for never leaving while a permit deadline is running?
next_actions: Check the expiry dates on both passports. Renew any passport that expires before Nov 1, 2027, so each has 6 months left after a spring 2027 trip. (@computer)

Email the Department of Tourism hosts team at hosts@tourism.gov.bt (phone +975 17661974) with 3 questions. Which SDF rate applies to nights after Aug 31, 2027 on a visa issued before then? Is a guide needed every day on a stay based in one certified homestay? What is the current visa extension procedure and fee? (@email)
Download the tentative 2027 festival dates from bhutan.travel/travel-trade. Mark 2-3 possible trip windows of 2-3 weeks between mid-March and the end of April 2027. (@computer)

Pick 3 licensed tour operators from services.bhutan.travel/search/tour-operator. Ask each for a written quote for two people, for 14 and 21 days in late March to April 2027, using certified village homestays, with a per-day cost breakdown. (@email)

List together every Bhutanese citizen either of you actually knows, how you met, and what proof you have, such as messages or photos. If the list is empty, cross off the personal-guest route. (@together)

Write a 150-word skills offer covering design, building, planting and your available dates. Email it to the Bhutan Foundation (info@bhutanfound.org) and the Tarayana Foundation (tarayana@tarayanafoundation.org, typed by hand and confirmed on +975 2 329-333). Ask whether a partner organization hosts skilled short-term volunteers, and under which visa category. (@email)

Email info@gmc.bt before paying NomadClub anything. Ask whether NomadClub is the authorized operator, whether holders are exempt from the SDF outside Gelephu, and whether one fee covers a married couple. (@email)
Add a calendar reminder for Mar 1, 2027: check bhutan.travel/announcements for the SDF rate after Aug 31, 2027. (@computer)
Call a travel-medicine clinic and book appointments for both of you in late January 2027, 6-8 weeks before a late-March departure. (@phone)

Once dates are set, enroll both of you in the Smart Traveler Enrollment Program (STEP) at step.state.gov. Confirm on travel.state.gov that the US Embassy in New Delhi covers US citizens in Bhutan. (@computer)
